max/grid: Pooling shrinks a channel. Split this four by four grid into two by two windows that do not overlap: a stride of two.
max/max: Max pooling keeps the largest value in each window: five, four, three and six.
max/out: The output is two by two: half as tall, half as wide, a quarter of the values.
max/map: Count rows and columns from zero. The three is output row one, column zero, and its window is input rows two and three, columns zero and one. Output row i reads input rows two i and two i plus one, and columns work the same way.
max/avg: Average pooling takes each window's mean instead: two point seven five, one point seven five, one point five and two point five.
shape/channels: Inputs often come as a stack of grids called channels, like the red, green and blue of a color image. Pooling runs on each channel on its own: sixteen channels of thirty two by thirty two become sixteen of sixteen by sixteen.
shape/formula: The size follows the output size formula, with F and S both two: thirty two minus two, over two, plus one, is sixteen.
shape/overlap: Windows can also overlap. Three by three windows with a stride of two share an edge column with the next. On twenty seven by twenty seven, that is twenty seven minus three, over two, plus one: thirteen.
shape/none: And there is nothing to learn: unlike a filter, pooling has no weights at all. Zero parameters.
shape/shift: When the grid is a filter's output, max pooling keeps how well the filter matched in each window, not exactly where. Move the five inside its window, and the output does not change.
